# Use Larger Axis Labels

## If you remember one thing

- Pay attention to axis labels, tick labels, and other annotations
- Chances are they are too small
- Most plotting software has poor defaults
- Using the defaults is almost certainly a poor choice

## Too small

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Axis labels, tick labels, and legend text are barely legible
- We see figures like this all the time

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-aus-athletes-small", fig_aus_athletes_small(),
          w = 5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Better, still too small

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Moving in the right direction
- But the figure is not balanced: text is small relative to the points

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-aus-athletes-ugly", fig_aus_athletes_ugly(),
          w = 5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Well balanced

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Text is clearly visible and fits the figure size
- Text and symbols scale together

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-aus-athletes-good", fig_aus_athletes_good(),
          w = 5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Too big

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Large text can be right if the figure will be shrunk
- But here the points are too small relative to the text

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-aus-athletes-big-ugly", fig_aus_athletes_big_ugly(),
          w = 5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Big and balanced

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Larger text and larger points
- Meant to be scaled down, where it looks just fine
- Test at the size at which the figure will actually be seen

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-aus-athletes-big-good", fig_aus_athletes_big_good(),
          w = 5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Why labels end up too small

- We preview figures large, on high-resolution monitors
- Small text looks fine at that size
- The figure is then shrunk to fit a page or slide
- Design for the final size
